rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.canonical_meaning: All lands of the public domain and natural resources belong to the State. Private ownership must rest on a valid State grant or on a legally recognized private right that predates the governing constitutional classification.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Public land and natural resources start as State property; a private claimant must show a lawful basis for ownership.
rows.required_concepts: ["State ownership is the starting presumption","private ownership requires a valid grant or recognized pre-existing right"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Public land and natural resources start as State property; a private claimant must show a lawful basis for ownership.","A materially equivalent statement of the Regalian Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Regalian Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The doctrine does not erase vested private rights. Only alienable lands of the public domain may generally be transferred, and only in the manner allowed by the Constitution and statutes.

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.canonical_meaning: The State may not be sued without its consent. Under the restrictive approach, immunity generally covers sovereign or governmental acts, while commercial or proprietary conduct may fall outside the protection; consent to suit is not automatically consent to execution.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Government cannot ordinarily be haled into court without consent, especially for sovereign acts, but commercial conduct and enforcement of a judgment require separate analysis.
rows.required_concepts: ["consent is ordinarily required","sovereign and commercial acts are distinguished","consent to suit differs from consent to execution"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Government cannot ordinarily be haled into court without consent, especially for sovereign acts, but commercial conduct and enforcement of a judgment require separate analysis.","A materially equivalent statement of the State Immunity from Suit is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the State Immunity from Suit.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Immunity may be expressly or impliedly waived, but waiver is strictly construed. Foreign-state immunity and immunity of agencies depend on the entity and the nature of the act.

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.canonical_meaning: An unconstitutional act is void, but before invalidation it may have produced consequences that equity and fairness require courts to recognize. The doctrine softens disruptive effects; it does not validate the unconstitutional act.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A void government act can still have past real-world effects that a court may preserve for fairness, without declaring the act valid.
rows.required_concepts: ["unconstitutional act remains void","past effects may exceptionally be recognized for equity","recognition does not validate the act"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A void government act can still have past real-world effects that a court may preserve for fairness, without declaring the act valid.","A materially equivalent statement of the Operative Fact Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Operative Fact Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Application is exceptional and fact-sensitive. It is not a license for officials to disregard the Constitution or a rule that every unconstitutional measure receives prospective-only treatment.

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.syllabus_topic: National Territory and Law of the Sea
rows.canonical_meaning: The Philippines is an archipelagic State whose islands and waters form one integrated unit, with archipelagic baselines measured under the Constitution, statute, and UNCLOS.
rows.plain_language_meaning: The islands and connecting waters are treated as one archipelago, subject to the law of the sea.
rows.required_concepts: ["the archipelago is treated as one integrated unit","baselines and maritime zones remain governed by UNCLOS and statute"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["The islands and connecting waters are treated as one archipelago, subject to the law of the sea.","A materially equivalent statement of the Archipelagic Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Archipelagic Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Archipelagic status does not eliminate internationally recognized navigation regimes or enlarge maritime zones beyond UNCLOS.

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.doctrine_title: Political Question Doctrine and Expanded Judicial Review
rows.canonical_meaning: Courts avoid questions textually committed to the political branches when no judicially manageable legal standard exists, but the 1987 Constitution requires review of grave abuse of discretion by any branch or instrumentality of government.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Some policy choices belong to elected branches, yet courts may still intervene when government gravely abuses its discretion.
rows.required_concepts: ["traditional political questions remain limited","grave abuse of discretion is judicially reviewable under the 1987 Constitution"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Some policy choices belong to elected branches, yet courts may still intervene when government gravely abuses its discretion.","A materially equivalent statement of the Political Question Doctrine and Expanded Judicial Review is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Political Question Doctrine and Expanded Judicial Review.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Expanded review does not make courts supervisors of every policy disagreement; an actual case and the other requisites of judicial review ordinarily remain necessary.

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.canonical_meaning: Legislative, executive, and judicial powers are allocated to separate branches, which may not usurp one another’s core functions, subject to the Constitution’s checks, balances, and instances of shared authority.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Each branch has its own central job, while constitutional checks keep any one branch from acting without limits.
rows.required_concepts: ["distinct core powers of the three branches","constitutional checks and balances qualify the separation"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Each branch has its own central job, while constitutional checks keep any one branch from acting without limits.","A materially equivalent statement of the Separation of Powers is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Separation of Powers.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The separation is functional, not absolute. The Constitution deliberately permits overlap in appointments, appropriations, impeachment, treaty concurrence, and judicial review.

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.canonical_meaning: Department secretaries are the President’s alter egos in matters within their departments, so their regular official acts are presumptively the President’s unless disapproved or constitutionally or statutorily assigned for personal presidential action.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A department secretary normally acts for the President, but not when the law requires the President personally to decide.
rows.required_concepts: ["department secretaries ordinarily act as presidential alter egos","personal or specially assigned presidential powers are excluded"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A department secretary normally acts for the President, but not when the law requires the President personally to decide.","A materially equivalent statement of the Qualified Political Agency Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Qualified Political Agency Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The doctrine does not automatically convert every act of a secretary serving ex officio on a separate corporate board into an act of the President.
rows.primary_authority: National Power Corporation Board of Directors v. Commission on Audit

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.canonical_meaning: Congress may not transfer its essential lawmaking power, but it may delegate authority to implement a complete law that supplies a sufficient standard, and the Constitution recognizes particular delegations such as tariff and emergency powers.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Congress must make the policy choices; an agency may fill in details when the law is complete and gives a workable standard.
rows.required_concepts: ["essential legislative power stays with Congress","valid delegation requires completeness and a sufficient standard"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Congress must make the policy choices; an agency may fill in details when the law is complete and gives a workable standard.","A materially equivalent statement of the Non-Delegation Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Non-Delegation Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Delegation is assessed in context, and standards may be express or fairly implied. Constitutionally authorized delegations and local or administrative implementation are not prohibited merely because discretion is involved.
rows.primary_authority: Tatad v. Secretary of the Department of Energy

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.canonical_meaning: Local autonomy gives local governments meaningful authority over local affairs, while the President exercises general supervision to ensure legality, not control to substitute presidential judgment for lawful local discretion.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Local governments may decide local matters within law; the President checks legality but ordinarily cannot replace their judgment with his or her own.
rows.required_concepts: ["local governments possess constitutionally protected autonomy","presidential supervision ensures legality and is not control"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Local governments may decide local matters within law; the President checks legality but ordinarily cannot replace their judgment with his or her own.","A materially equivalent statement of the Local Autonomy and General Supervision is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Local Autonomy and General Supervision.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Local autonomy is not sovereignty. Congress may define local powers within constitutional limits, and national intervention is valid where the Constitution or a statute lawfully authorizes it.
rows.primary_authority: Kilusang Mayo Uno v. Aurora Pacific Economic Zone and Freeport Authority

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.canonical_meaning: Executive privilege protects narrowly defined confidential presidential, military, diplomatic, national-security, and deliberative communications when disclosure would impair public functions; the claim must identify the protected information and is qualified, not absolute.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Some high-level government communications may remain confidential, but the government must justify the claim and courts can weigh competing constitutional needs.
rows.required_concepts: ["privilege protects specified confidential governmental communications","the claim is qualified and must be properly invoked"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Some high-level government communications may remain confidential, but the government must justify the claim and courts can weigh competing constitutional needs.","A materially equivalent statement of the Executive Privilege is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Executive Privilege.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: A generalized interest in secrecy is insufficient. Demonstrated need in criminal justice or constitutional oversight may overcome the privilege, depending on the information and context.
rows.primary_authority: Neri v. Senate Committee on Accountability of Public Officers and Investigations

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.canonical_meaning: A party ordinarily must use available and adequate administrative remedies before seeking judicial relief, allowing the agency to correct errors and apply its expertise.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Normally, a person must first complete the agency process before going to court.
rows.required_concepts: ["available administrative remedies are ordinarily pursued first","the rule respects agency correction and expertise"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Normally, a person must first complete the agency process before going to court.","A materially equivalent statement of the Exhaustion of Administrative Remedies is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Exhaustion of Administrative Remedies.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Recognized exceptions include pure legal or constitutional questions, patent illegality, irreparable injury, denial of due process, estoppel, unreasonable delay, futility, and other circumstances making the remedy inadequate.

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.canonical_meaning: When a claim is originally cognizable in court but its resolution requires an agency’s specialized competence on an issue committed to that agency, the court may defer until the agency has addressed the issue.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A court may pause a case so the expert agency can decide a technical issue first.
rows.required_concepts: ["court and agency may both have roles","the agency first resolves an issue within its special competence"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A court may pause a case so the expert agency can decide a technical issue first.","A materially equivalent statement of the Primary Jurisdiction Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Primary Jurisdiction Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Primary jurisdiction differs from exhaustion: it applies even when the court has jurisdiction. It does not apply when the issue is purely legal or agency expertise is unnecessary.
rows.primary_authority: Euro-Med Laboratories Phil., Inc. v. Province of Batangas

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.canonical_meaning: Generally accepted principles of international law form part of Philippine law without need of separate legislation, but treaties and customary rules operate within the constitutional allocation of powers.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Widely accepted international-law principles can apply domestically even without a new statute.
rows.required_concepts: ["generally accepted international-law principles are incorporated","domestic constitutional limits still govern their operation"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Widely accepted international-law principles can apply domestically even without a new statute.","A materially equivalent statement of the Incorporation Clause is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Incorporation Clause.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Not every international statement or practice is a generally accepted principle. A conflicting constitutional command controls domestically.

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.canonical_meaning: Treaties in force bind the parties and must be performed in good faith; a State generally may not invoke its internal law as justification for failing to perform its treaty obligations.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A country must honor its valid treaties in good faith.
rows.required_concepts: ["valid treaties are binding","performance must be in good faith"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A country must honor its valid treaties in good faith.","A materially equivalent statement of the Pacta Sunt Servanda is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Pacta Sunt Servanda.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Domestic enforceability depends on constitutional processes, treaty text, and whether provisions are self-executing. A treaty cannot amend the Constitution.

rows.subject: Political and Public International Law
rows.canonical_meaning: By entering a valid treaty, a sovereign State may voluntarily accept limits on the exercise of its powers; that consent is itself an exercise, not a surrender, of sovereignty.
rows.plain_language_meaning: The Philippines may lawfully agree to treaty limits because choosing those commitments is an act of sovereignty.
rows.required_concepts: ["treaty limits may be voluntarily accepted","voluntary limitation is an exercise of sovereignty"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["The Philippines may lawfully agree to treaty limits because choosing those commitments is an act of sovereignty.","A materially equivalent statement of the Auto-Limitation of Sovereignty is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Auto-Limitation of Sovereignty.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Only commitments validly made under the Constitution bind the State domestically, and constitutional supremacy remains.

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: A corporation has a juridical personality separate and distinct from its stockholders, members, and officers; its property, debts, and acts are ordinarily its own.
rows.plain_language_meaning: The corporation is legally separate from the people who own or manage it.
rows.required_concepts: ["the corporation is a separate juridical person","corporate assets and liabilities ordinarily do not belong to owners personally"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["The corporation is legally separate from the people who own or manage it.","A materially equivalent statement of the Separate Juridical Personality is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Separate Juridical Personality.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Separate personality may be disregarded only on established grounds; limited liability does not protect a person from liability for that person’s own tort, crime, bad faith, or statutory breach.
rows.primary_authority: Revised Corporation Code of the Philippines

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: Courts may disregard corporate personality when it is used to defeat public convenience, justify wrong, protect fraud, or serve as the mere alter ego or instrumentality of another, upon clear proof of the controlling facts.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A court may look past a sham company used to commit fraud or avoid a legal duty.
rows.required_concepts: ["corporate personality is exceptionally disregarded","fraud, evasion, or alter-ego misuse must be shown"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A court may look past a sham company used to commit fraud or avoid a legal duty.","A materially equivalent statement of the Piercing the Corporate Veil is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Piercing the Corporate Veil.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Piercing is applied with caution and for the particular obligation at issue; ownership or control alone is insufficient.

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: Subscribed capital and corporate assets are treated as a trust fund for payment of corporate creditors, so distributions that impair capital or transfers designed to defeat creditors may be recovered as law permits.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Corporate capital should remain available to creditors before owners take it out.
rows.required_concepts: ["corporate capital protects creditors","improper distributions or transfers may be recovered"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Corporate capital should remain available to creditors before owners take it out.","A materially equivalent statement of the Trust Fund Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Trust Fund Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The doctrine does not make every shareholder personally liable for all corporate debt; liability depends on the unlawful distribution, unpaid subscription, fraud, or applicable statute.

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: Courts ordinarily do not substitute their judgment for an informed, good-faith decision of disinterested directors made within corporate powers and with due care.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Judges usually will not second-guess an honest, informed board business decision.
rows.required_concepts: ["board decision is informed and in good faith","courts ordinarily defer rather than substitute business judgment"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Judges usually will not second-guess an honest, informed board business decision.","A materially equivalent statement of the Business Judgment Rule is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Business Judgment Rule.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Deference does not cover fraud, bad faith, gross negligence, self-dealing, illegality, oppression, or acts beyond corporate authority.
rows.primary_authority: Revised Corporation Code of the Philippines

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: A corporation may be bound by an officer’s act when it knowingly permits that officer to appear authorized and a third person reasonably and in good faith relies on the appearance.
rows.plain_language_meaning: If the company created a reasonable appearance that its officer could act, it may be bound to an innocent third party who relied on that appearance.
rows.required_concepts: ["the corporation created or tolerated an appearance of authority","the third party reasonably relied in good faith"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["If the company created a reasonable appearance that its officer could act, it may be bound to an innocent third party who relied on that appearance.","A materially equivalent statement of the Apparent Authority is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Apparent Authority.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The officer cannot create apparent authority by self-serving assertions alone; the appearance must be traceable to the corporation.
rows.primary_authority: Agro Food Products, Inc. v. Vitarich Corporation

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: A person who knowingly acts as, or deals with, an ostensible corporation may be barred from denying its corporate existence to escape obligations arising from that dealing.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Someone who treated a business as a corporation cannot later deny it only to avoid the bargain.
rows.required_concepts: ["knowing conduct as or with an ostensible corporation","estoppel prevents an inconsistent denial to evade the resulting obligation"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Someone who treated a business as a corporation cannot later deny it only to avoid the bargain.","A materially equivalent statement of the Corporation by Estoppel is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Corporation by Estoppel.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The doctrine does not create a corporation for all purposes, legalize a prohibited enterprise, or bind a person who did not knowingly deal on that basis.
rows.primary_authority: Missionary Sisters of Our Lady of Fatima v. Alzona

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: An unlicensed foreign corporation barred from suing because it is doing business in the Philippines may nevertheless sue on an isolated transaction that does not show continuity of commercial dealings here.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A one-off Philippine transaction generally does not by itself trigger the license-based bar to suit.
rows.required_concepts: ["doing business implies continuity of commercial dealings","an isolated transaction may be enforced despite lack of license"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A one-off Philippine transaction generally does not by itself trigger the license-based bar to suit.","A materially equivalent statement of the Isolated Transaction Rule is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Isolated Transaction Rule.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Whether dealings are isolated depends on substance, continuity, and the corporation’s ordinary business; the rule does not excuse licensing when business is actually being conducted here.
rows.primary_authority: Steelcase, Inc. v. Design International Selections, Inc.

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.doctrine_title: Limited Liability Doctrine in Maritime Law
rows.canonical_meaning: A vessel owner’s liability for specified maritime obligations may be limited to the owner’s interest in the vessel, freight, and appurtenances under the real-and-hypothecary nature of maritime law.
rows.plain_language_meaning: In qualifying maritime claims, the vessel owner may abandon the vessel and freight and limit liability to that maritime value.
rows.required_concepts: ["maritime liability may be limited to vessel and freight","the rule arises from real and hypothecary maritime liability"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["In qualifying maritime claims, the vessel owner may abandon the vessel and freight and limit liability to that maritime value.","A materially equivalent statement of the Limited Liability Doctrine in Maritime Law is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Limited Liability Doctrine in Maritime Law.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The limitation is unavailable in recognized situations such as the owner’s own fault or negligence, lack of seaworthiness attributable to the owner, or obligations governed by a different law or contract.
rows.primary_authority: Monarch Insurance Co., Inc. v. Court of Appeals

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: Common carriers must exercise extraordinary diligence over passengers and goods, measured by all the circumstances, and statutory presumptions may arise from injury, death, loss, or damage.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A business carrying the public must use a very high level of care for passengers and cargo.
rows.required_concepts: ["common carriers owe extraordinary diligence","liability and presumptions depend on the passenger or goods context"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A business carrying the public must use a very high level of care for passengers and cargo.","A materially equivalent statement of the Extraordinary Diligence of Common Carriers is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Extraordinary Diligence of Common Carriers.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The carrier is not an absolute insurer. Fortuitous events and statutory defenses may apply only when their elements, including required carrier care, are proved.

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: Insurance is a contract of utmost good faith: each party, especially the applicant regarding material risk facts, must disclose matters required by law, and material concealment or misrepresentation may permit rescission.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Insurance depends on honest disclosure of important risk facts; hiding a material fact can defeat the policy.
rows.required_concepts: ["utmost good faith governs insurance","material concealment or misrepresentation may justify rescission"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Insurance depends on honest disclosure of important risk facts; hiding a material fact can defeat the policy.","A materially equivalent statement of the Uberrimae Fidei in Insurance is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Uberrimae Fidei in Insurance.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The fact must be material under the Code, and waiver, incontestability, the insurer’s knowledge, or statutory rules may change the result.

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: A holder in due course takes a complete and regular negotiable instrument for value, in good faith, before it is overdue, and without notice of infirmity or defect, and generally holds it free from personal defenses but subject to real defenses.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A qualifying good-faith holder of a negotiable instrument is protected from many defenses between earlier parties, but not from the strongest real defenses.
rows.required_concepts: ["statutory holder-in-due-course elements","personal defenses are cut off while real defenses remain"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A qualifying good-faith holder of a negotiable instrument is protected from many defenses between earlier parties, but not from the strongest real defenses.","A materially equivalent statement of the Holder in Due Course Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Holder in Due Course Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: A transferee who fails any statutory element may still have ordinary holder rights but not holder-in-due-course protection.

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: Trademark infringement is assessed by whether the dominant features of the marks are so similar that confusion or deception is likely, considering the marks as encountered by ordinary purchasers.
rows.plain_language_meaning: The comparison focuses on the memorable, dominant parts of the marks and whether buyers are likely to be confused.
rows.required_concepts: ["dominant features are compared","likely consumer confusion is the controlling concern"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["The comparison focuses on the memorable, dominant parts of the marks and whether buyers are likely to be confused.","A materially equivalent statement of the Dominancy Test is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Dominancy Test.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The marks are considered in their marketplace context, not by mechanical side-by-side dissection alone; the holistic test under current law may also be relevant.
rows.primary_authority: Dermaline, Inc. v. Myra Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: Taxes are indispensable to government, so collection remedies are construed to protect the revenue; nevertheless, taxation and assessment must comply strictly with statutory authority and constitutional due process.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Government needs taxes to operate, but urgency does not excuse unlawful assessment or denial of due process.
rows.required_concepts: ["taxes are essential to government","revenue collection remains bounded by statute and due process"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Government needs taxes to operate, but urgency does not excuse unlawful assessment or denial of due process.","A materially equivalent statement of the Lifeblood Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Lifeblood Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The maxim does not cure lack of notice, an invalid assessment, or disregard of taxpayer rights.
rows.primary_authority: Commissioner of Internal Revenue v. Metro Star Superama, Inc.

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: A claimant must point to a clear legal grant of tax exemption; doubts are generally resolved against exemption and in favor of taxation.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A taxpayer claiming exemption needs clear legal language granting it.
rows.required_concepts: ["exemption must be clearly granted by law","ambiguity ordinarily favors taxation"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A taxpayer claiming exemption needs clear legal language granting it.","A materially equivalent statement of the Strict Construction of Tax Exemptions is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Strict Construction of Tax Exemptions.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The rule does not convert a tax-imposition provision into a broad levy, and different construction may apply to constitutionally exempt entities or refunds of taxes collected without legal basis.
rows.primary_authority: Sea-Land Service, Inc. v. Court of Appeals

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.doctrine_title: No Set-Off of Taxes Against Government Claims
rows.canonical_meaning: Taxes generally cannot be set off against a taxpayer’s claim against the government because the obligations do not arise between parties acting in the same capacity and taxes are public obligations, not ordinary debts.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A taxpayer usually cannot cancel a tax bill by pointing to money the government allegedly owes it.
rows.required_concepts: ["taxes are not ordinary contractual debts","legal compensation ordinarily does not apply"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A taxpayer usually cannot cancel a tax bill by pointing to money the government allegedly owes it.","A materially equivalent statement of the No Set-Off of Taxes Against Government Claims is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the No Set-Off of Taxes Against Government Claims.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Set-off may occur where a statute expressly authorizes it or where both obligations have become liquidated and demandable in a setting recognized by law.
rows.primary_authority: Philex Mining Corporation v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: A tax assessment must follow the notice, factual-and-legal explanation, opportunity-to-respond, authority, and timing requirements prescribed by the tax law and regulations; a material denial of due process may invalidate it.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Tax authorities must tell the taxpayer the basis of an assessment and follow the required process.
rows.required_concepts: ["required notice and reasons must be provided","the taxpayer receives the prescribed opportunity to respond"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Tax authorities must tell the taxpayer the basis of an assessment and follow the required process.","A materially equivalent statement of the Due Process in Tax Assessment is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Due Process in Tax Assessment.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Not every procedural defect is jurisdictional; the consequence depends on the governing statute, regulation, and whether the defect materially denied the mandated process.
rows.primary_authority: Commissioner of Internal Revenue v. Metro Star Superama, Inc.

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: Philippine VAT generally taxes consumption in the Philippines; exports and qualifying foreign-consumption transactions may receive zero-rating only when statutory conditions are satisfied.
rows.plain_language_meaning: VAT is aimed at Philippine consumption, so true exports may be zero-rated if the law’s requirements are met.
rows.required_concepts: ["VAT follows the place of consumption","zero-rating requires the statutory elements"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["VAT is aimed at Philippine consumption, so true exports may be zero-rated if the law’s requirements are met.","A materially equivalent statement of the Destination Principle in VAT is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Destination Principle in VAT.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The destination principle does not itself create a refund or zero-rating; the transaction must fit the current NIRC provision and documentary requirements.
rows.primary_authority: Placer Dome Technical Services (Philippines), Inc. v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: The source of income is the property, activity, or service that produced the income, not merely the place where payment was made or received; the NIRC’s source rules govern each income class.
rows.plain_language_meaning: To locate income for tax purposes, ask what activity or property earned it, not simply where the money was paid.
rows.required_concepts: ["source means the income-producing activity or property","statutory source rules control"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["To locate income for tax purposes, ask what activity or property earned it, not simply where the money was paid.","A materially equivalent statement of the Source-of-Income Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Source-of-Income Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Different categories such as services, interest, rent, royalties, and sales have distinct statutory source tests.
rows.primary_authority: Commissioner of Internal Revenue v. Baier-Nickel

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.doctrine_title: Strict Proof in Tax Refund Claims
rows.canonical_meaning: A taxpayer seeking a refund must prove entitlement under the governing statutory ground and comply with the applicable administrative, judicial, prescriptive, and evidentiary requirements.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A refund claimant must prove both the legal basis and the required filings and documents.
rows.required_concepts: ["claimant bears the burden of proving entitlement","statutory deadlines and proof requirements matter"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A refund claimant must prove both the legal basis and the required filings and documents.","A materially equivalent statement of the Strict Proof in Tax Refund Claims is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Strict Proof in Tax Refund Claims.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: A refund based on an erroneous or illegal exaction is not always treated like a legislative tax exemption; courts distinguish the nature of the claim and construe the tax-imposition provision accordingly.
rows.primary_authority: Petron Corporation v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue

rows.subject: Commercial and Taxation Laws
rows.canonical_meaning: A revocation, modification, or reversal of a BIR ruling generally may not be applied retroactively to a taxpayer’s prejudice, except in the statutory situations involving material misstatement, materially different facts, or bad faith.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A taxpayer who honestly relied on a BIR ruling is usually protected from a later adverse change for the earlier period.
rows.required_concepts: ["adverse reversal is generally prospective","statutory bad-faith and misinformation exceptions apply"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A taxpayer who honestly relied on a BIR ruling is usually protected from a later adverse change for the earlier period.","A materially equivalent statement of the Non-Retroactivity of Adverse BIR Rulings is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Non-Retroactivity of Adverse BIR Rulings.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Protection depends on actual good-faith reliance and substantially identical facts; it does not perpetuate a treatment after the taxpayer receives valid notice of the change.
rows.primary_authority: Commissioner of Internal Revenue v. San Roque Power Corporation

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: A person must exercise rights and perform duties with justice, honesty, and good faith; a legal right exercised solely or chiefly to injure another may create liability under Articles 19, 20, and 21 of the Civil Code.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Having a right does not permit using it dishonestly or just to harm someone.
rows.required_concepts: ["a legal right must be exercised in good faith","abusive exercise that causes injury may create liability"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Having a right does not permit using it dishonestly or just to harm someone.","A materially equivalent statement of the Abuse of Rights Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Abuse of Rights Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Bad faith or an abusive manner must be proved; loss caused by the ordinary, proper exercise of a right is not enough.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: Psychological incapacity is a legal, not medical, concept: a durable aspect of personality existing at the time of marriage must make a spouse genuinely unable, not merely unwilling, to perform essential marital obligations; clear and convincing evidence is required, but expert testimony is not indispensable.
rows.plain_language_meaning: The ground is a serious, enduring inability rooted in the spouse’s personality when the marriage began—not ordinary incompatibility or refusal—and it need not be proved by a psychiatrist.
rows.required_concepts: ["legal rather than medical concept","juridical antecedence, gravity, and durability","genuine inability to perform essential obligations","clear and convincing evidence; expert testimony not mandatory"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["The ground is a serious, enduring inability rooted in the spouse’s personality when the marriage began—not ordinary incompatibility or refusal—and it need not be proved by a psychiatrist.","A materially equivalent statement of the Psychological Incapacity under Tan-Andal is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Psychological Incapacity under Tan-Andal.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The inquiry is fact-specific and must identify the essential obligation not performed. Difficulty, immaturity, infidelity, or separation alone does not automatically establish incapacity.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: Contracts generally bind only the parties, their assigns, and heirs, subject to the nature of the obligation, stipulation, or law; a valid stipulation pour autrui may benefit a third person who accepts before revocation.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A contract normally affects its parties, not strangers, with limited legal exceptions.
rows.required_concepts: ["contracts generally bind the parties and successors","third persons are affected only under recognized exceptions"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A contract normally affects its parties, not strangers, with limited legal exceptions.","A materially equivalent statement of the Relativity of Contracts is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Relativity of Contracts.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Heirs are not liable beyond inherited property. Third-party beneficiary, real-right, fraud, and inducement rules must be separately established.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: Parties may establish terms they deem convenient provided those terms are not contrary to law, morals, good customs, public order, or public policy.
rows.plain_language_meaning: People may shape their bargain, but not by terms the legal system forbids.
rows.required_concepts: ["freedom to set contract terms","mandatory law and public norms limit that freedom"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["People may shape their bargain, but not by terms the legal system forbids.","A materially equivalent statement of the Autonomy of Contracts is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Autonomy of Contracts.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Consent and a written clause do not validate an illegal, unconscionable, or otherwise prohibited stipulation.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: A contract must bind both parties, and its validity or performance may not be left solely to the will of one party.
rows.plain_language_meaning: One side cannot reserve an unrestricted power to decide whether the bargain will bind or be performed.
rows.required_concepts: ["both parties are bound","validity or performance cannot depend solely on one party’s will"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["One side cannot reserve an unrestricted power to decide whether the bargain will bind or be performed.","A materially equivalent statement of the Mutuality of Contracts is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Mutuality of Contracts.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: A third person may determine performance under Article 1309, and objective adjustment mechanisms are valid when they do not give one party uncontrolled discretion.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.doctrine_title: Rebus Sic Stantibus and Extraordinary Difficulty
rows.canonical_meaning: When performance of a service becomes so extraordinarily difficult as to be manifestly beyond what the parties contemplated, Article 1267 may release the obligor in whole or in part.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A truly extraordinary, unforeseeable change may justify relief when performance becomes far beyond the bargain—not merely more expensive.
rows.required_concepts: ["extraordinary difficulty beyond contemplation","possible whole or partial relief"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A truly extraordinary, unforeseeable change may justify relief when performance becomes far beyond the bargain—not merely more expensive.","A materially equivalent statement of the Rebus Sic Stantibus and Extraordinary Difficulty is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Rebus Sic Stantibus and Extraordinary Difficulty.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The doctrine is exceptional, applies narrowly, and does not excuse ordinary business risk, predictable price changes, or simple inconvenience.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: Foreign law is a question of fact that must be pleaded and proved; when it is not properly established, Philippine courts may presume it is the same as Philippine law.
rows.plain_language_meaning: If a party fails to prove the relevant foreign law, the court may apply Philippine law as though the two were the same.
rows.required_concepts: ["foreign law must be pleaded and proved","unproved foreign law may be presumed identical to Philippine law"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["If a party fails to prove the relevant foreign law, the court may apply Philippine law as though the two were the same.","A materially equivalent statement of the Processual Presumption is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Processual Presumption.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The presumption does not apply when the court may properly take judicial notice or when a treaty or rule supplies another method of proof.
rows.primary_authority: Wildvalley Shipping Co., Ltd. v. Court of Appeals

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: Philippine laws on family rights and duties, status, condition, and legal capacity bind Filipino citizens even abroad, and the intrinsic validity of testamentary and intestate succession follows the decedent’s national law.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A Filipino’s personal status and a decedent’s succession rules generally follow nationality even when events occur abroad.
rows.required_concepts: ["nationality governs specified personal matters","succession follows the decedent’s national law for intrinsic validity"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A Filipino’s personal status and a decedent’s succession rules generally follow nationality even when events occur abroad.","A materially equivalent statement of the Nationality Principle is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Nationality Principle.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Form of acts, property rules, renvoi, public policy, and specific statutes may require separate conflict-of-laws analysis.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: A child conceived or born during a valid marriage is presumed legitimate, and legitimacy may be impugned only by the proper party, on statutory grounds, and within the prescribed period.
rows.plain_language_meaning: The law strongly presumes a child born during marriage is legitimate, and only a timely statutory challenge can rebut it.
rows.required_concepts: ["birth or conception during marriage triggers the presumption","challenge is restricted by standing, grounds, and time"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["The law strongly presumes a child born during marriage is legitimate, and only a timely statutory challenge can rebut it.","A materially equivalent statement of the Presumption of Legitimacy is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Presumption of Legitimacy.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The applicable Family Code provisions depend on dates of birth, separation, and remarriage; genetic evidence does not eliminate the statutory procedural requirements.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: An obligor is generally not liable for a loss caused solely by an unforeseeable or unavoidable event independent of human will, unless law, stipulation, the nature of the obligation, assumption of risk, delay, or the obligor’s concurrent negligence makes liability attach.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A true unavoidable event may excuse liability only when the debtor did not help cause the loss and no special rule shifts the risk.
rows.required_concepts: ["event is unforeseeable or unavoidable and independent","no concurrent fault or applicable risk-shifting rule"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A true unavoidable event may excuse liability only when the debtor did not help cause the loss and no special rule shifts the risk.","A materially equivalent statement of the Fortuitous Event Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Fortuitous Event Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: A fortuitous event is not a defense when negligence concurs, the debtor is in delay, the obligation is generic, or law or contract assigns the risk.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: Proximate cause is the cause which, in a natural and continuous sequence unbroken by an efficient intervening cause, produces the injury and without which the result would not have occurred.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Liability tracks the legally significant cause that naturally led to the injury without a new independent cause breaking the chain.
rows.required_concepts: ["natural and continuous causal sequence","no efficient intervening cause","injury would not otherwise have occurred"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Liability tracks the legally significant cause that naturally led to the injury without a new independent cause breaking the chain.","A materially equivalent statement of the Proximate Cause is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Proximate Cause.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Factual cause alone is insufficient; contributory negligence, superseding cause, and the duty and scope of risk still matter.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: Even where both parties were negligent, the party who had the final clear opportunity to avoid the injury but failed to do so may bear liability under the doctrine’s strict requisites.
rows.plain_language_meaning: The person who still had a real final chance to prevent the accident may be liable despite the other person’s earlier negligence.
rows.required_concepts: ["both parties were negligent in sequence","one had a later clear and effective opportunity to avoid harm"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["The person who still had a real final chance to prevent the accident may be liable despite the other person’s earlier negligence.","A materially equivalent statement of the Last Clear Chance Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Last Clear Chance Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The doctrine is generally confined to suitable quasi-delict settings, requires a genuinely later opportunity, and does not override statutory rules or automatically defeat contractual common-carrier liability.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: No person may unjustly enrich himself or herself at another’s expense; restitution may follow when one receives a benefit without a valid legal ground and the other suffers a corresponding loss.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A person should not keep a benefit unfairly obtained at someone else’s expense without a legal basis.
rows.required_concepts: ["benefit to one and corresponding loss to another","absence of a valid legal ground"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A person should not keep a benefit unfairly obtained at someone else’s expense without a legal basis.","A materially equivalent statement of the Unjust Enrichment is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Unjust Enrichment.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The doctrine is subsidiary and cannot defeat an express contract or statute that validly allocates the benefit or risk.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: When parties are equally at fault in an illegal agreement, courts generally leave them where they are and deny recovery under the agreement.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Courts usually will not help either equally guilty party enforce or unwind an illegal bargain.
rows.required_concepts: ["both parties share fault in an illegal transaction","courts generally deny affirmative relief"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Courts usually will not help either equally guilty party enforce or unwind an illegal bargain.","A materially equivalent statement of the In Pari Delicto is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the In Pari Delicto.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Statutory exceptions, unequal guilt, protection of a favored class, repudiation before the illegal purpose, and overriding public policy may permit recovery.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: A seller generally cannot transfer better title than the seller has.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Someone who does not own or have authority over property normally cannot give a buyer valid ownership of it.
rows.required_concepts: ["transferor generally cannot convey better title","buyer ordinarily takes subject to the true owner’s right"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Someone who does not own or have authority over property normally cannot give a buyer valid ownership of it.","A materially equivalent statement of the Nemo Dat Quod Non Habet is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Nemo Dat Quod Non Habet.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Estoppel, agency, negotiable-document rules, statutory sales, and other specific protections for good-faith purchasers may create exceptions.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.doctrine_title: Builder in Good Faith under Article 448
rows.canonical_meaning: When a person in good faith builds, plants, or sows on another’s land, the landowner must choose between appropriation after paying the statutory indemnity and compelling purchase or rent as Article 448 allows; the landowner cannot simply take the improvement for free.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A good-faith builder on another’s land triggers a statutory choice and compensation process for the landowner.
rows.required_concepts: ["builder and landowner must initially be in good faith","landowner has the statutory options","indemnity precedes appropriation"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A good-faith builder on another’s land triggers a statutory choice and compensation process for the landowner.","A materially equivalent statement of the Builder in Good Faith under Article 448 is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Builder in Good Faith under Article 448.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Different rules apply when either party acted in bad faith, and compelled purchase is unavailable when land value is considerably greater than the improvement.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: A purchaser in good faith may generally rely on the face of a clean transfer certificate of title and need not investigate beyond it absent facts that should prompt inquiry.
rows.plain_language_meaning: An ordinary good-faith buyer may trust a clean title unless warning signs call for investigation.
rows.required_concepts: ["good-faith purchaser may rely on clean title","notice or red flags create a duty to inquire"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["An ordinary good-faith buyer may trust a clean title unless warning signs call for investigation.","A materially equivalent statement of the Mirror Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Mirror Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The protection is unavailable to a buyer with actual or constructive notice, suspicious circumstances, knowledge of another’s possession, or the heightened diligence expected of banks and similar institutions.
rows.primary_authority: Spouses Manalese v. Estate of Ferreras

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.doctrine_title: Indefeasibility Is Not a Shield for Fraud
rows.canonical_meaning: A Torrens title is strong evidence of ownership, but registration does not validate a forged or fraudulent transfer or permit the registrant to use the system as an instrument of fraud.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A land title protects ownership; it does not turn forgery or fraud into a valid transfer.
rows.required_concepts: ["registration does not cure forgery or fraud","Torrens system cannot be used to perpetrate fraud"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A land title protects ownership; it does not turn forgery or fraud into a valid transfer.","A materially equivalent statement of the Indefeasibility Is Not a Shield for Fraud is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Indefeasibility Is Not a Shield for Fraud.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: An innocent purchaser for value may acquire statutory protection in appropriate circumstances, and actions are subject to the applicable remedy, prescription, and laches rules.

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: An innocent purchaser for value buys property for fair consideration without actual or constructive notice of another’s right and after the diligence reasonably demanded by the circumstances.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Protection goes to a buyer who paid value, lacked notice, and reasonably checked warning signs.
rows.required_concepts: ["valuable consideration","good faith and absence of notice","reasonable diligence"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Protection goes to a buyer who paid value, lacked notice, and reasonably checked warning signs.","A materially equivalent statement of the Innocent Purchaser for Value is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Innocent Purchaser for Value.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Good faith is a factual issue; visible possession by another, title annotations, irregular documents, undervalue, and institutional-buyer status may require further inquiry.
rows.primary_authority: Spouses Manalese v. Estate of Ferreras

rows.subject: Civil Law and Land Titles and Deeds
rows.canonical_meaning: When property is acquired or held through fraud, mistake, breach of confidence, or circumstances recognized by the Civil Code, an implied trust may oblige the registered holder to reconvey it to the beneficial owner.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A person holding title may be required to return property when fairness and the Civil Code treat that person as holding it for the true beneficiary.
rows.required_concepts: ["circumstances create a resulting or constructive trust","reconveyance restores the beneficial owner rather than erasing the title system"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A person holding title may be required to return property when fairness and the Civil Code treat that person as holding it for the true beneficiary.","A materially equivalent statement of the Implied Trust and Reconveyance is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Implied Trust and Reconveyance.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The claimant must prove the trust and ownership basis, and prescription, laches, repudiation, and innocent-purchaser rights vary with the kind of trust and possession.

rows.subject: Labor Law and Social Legislation
rows.canonical_meaning: Employment is assessed through selection and engagement, payment of wages, power of dismissal, and especially the employer’s power to control the means and methods of the work.
rows.plain_language_meaning: The strongest sign of employment is whether the alleged employer may direct how the work is done.
rows.required_concepts: ["four indicators of employment","control over means and methods is generally most important"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["The strongest sign of employment is whether the alleged employer may direct how the work is done.","A materially equivalent statement of the Four-Fold Test is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Four-Fold Test.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: No single label or contract clause controls; the actual relationship and, where appropriate, the economic-dependence analysis must be considered.
rows.primary_authority: Escauriaga v. Fitness First Phil., Inc.

rows.subject: Labor Law and Social Legislation
rows.canonical_meaning: Where the control test is insufficient, courts consider the totality of circumstances and whether the worker is economically dependent on the alleged employer for continued work in the business.
rows.plain_language_meaning: If day-to-day control is unclear, the court asks whether the worker is really operating an independent business or depends on this employer for livelihood.
rows.required_concepts: ["control is examined first","economic dependence and totality of circumstances supplement the analysis"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["If day-to-day control is unclear, the court asks whether the worker is really operating an independent business or depends on this employer for livelihood.","A materially equivalent statement of the Two-Tiered Test and Economic Dependence is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Two-Tiered Test and Economic Dependence.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Economic dependence is not a wage-level test and does not replace the statutory treatment of clearly defined work arrangements.

rows.subject: Labor Law and Social Legislation
rows.canonical_meaning: Labor-only contracting exists when the contractor lacks the required substantial capital or investment or the workers perform activities directly related to the principal’s main business, together with the control and statutory circumstances specified by labor law; the principal is treated as the employer for liability purposes.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A manpower middleman without a real independent business may leave the principal legally responsible as employer.
rows.required_concepts: ["contractor is not genuinely independent under statutory factors","principal may be treated as employer"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A manpower middleman without a real independent business may leave the principal legally responsible as employer.","A materially equivalent statement of the Labor-Only Contracting is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Labor-Only Contracting.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Legitimate job contracting remains allowed when the contractor carries an independent business, has the required resources, controls its work, and complies with labor standards.

rows.subject: Labor Law and Social Legislation
rows.canonical_meaning: An employer may regulate business operations and workforce matters, but its prerogatives must be exercised in good faith, for legitimate business purposes, and consistently with law, contract, collective bargaining agreements, and fair play.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Management may run the business, but not arbitrarily or in violation of worker rights.
rows.required_concepts: ["employer retains legitimate operational discretion","good faith and legal or contractual limits apply"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Management may run the business, but not arbitrarily or in violation of worker rights.","A materially equivalent statement of the Management Prerogative is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Management Prerogative.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The phrase is not an independent defense to discrimination, union interference, wage violations, or disproportionate discipline.
rows.primary_authority: Philex Gold Philippines, Inc. v. Philex Bulawan Supervisors Union

rows.subject: Labor Law and Social Legislation
rows.canonical_meaning: An employer may not unilaterally eliminate or reduce a benefit that has become a deliberate, consistent, and long-standing company practice, unless the benefit arose from error or another recognized legal basis prevents vesting.
rows.plain_language_meaning: A regular benefit intentionally given over time may become protected from unilateral reduction.
rows.required_concepts: ["benefit is deliberate, consistent, and long-standing","unilateral diminution is prohibited"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["A regular benefit intentionally given over time may become protected from unilateral reduction.","A materially equivalent statement of the Non-Diminution of Benefits is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Non-Diminution of Benefits.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The employee must prove the practice; sporadic, conditional, negotiated, productivity-based, or mistaken payments do not automatically become vested benefits.
rows.primary_authority: Eastern Telecommunications Philippines, Inc. v. Eastern Telecoms Employees Union

rows.subject: Labor Law and Social Legislation
rows.canonical_meaning: For just-cause dismissal, the employer must give a first written notice specifying the charges and a reasonable chance to answer, then, after considering the defense, a second written notice stating the decision and grounds.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Before a just-cause firing, the worker must receive written charges, a fair chance to explain, and a written final decision.
rows.required_concepts: ["specific first notice and opportunity to respond","reasoned second notice after consideration"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Before a just-cause firing, the worker must receive written charges, a fair chance to explain, and a written final decision.","A materially equivalent statement of the Twin-Notice Rule is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Twin-Notice Rule.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The required process differs for authorized-cause termination. A valid substantive cause may avoid reinstatement even when procedural due process was defective, but statutory damages may result.
rows.primary_authority: King of Kings Transport, Inc. v. Mamac

rows.subject: Labor Law and Social Legislation
rows.doctrine_title: Burden of Proof in Dismissal Cases
rows.canonical_meaning: The employee first proves the fact of dismissal when disputed; once dismissal is shown, the employer bears the burden of proving a valid cause and compliance with due process.
rows.plain_language_meaning: The worker proves that firing happened; the employer then must justify it and show fair procedure.
rows.required_concepts: ["employee proves disputed fact of dismissal","employer proves valid cause and due process after dismissal is shown"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["The worker proves that firing happened; the employer then must justify it and show fair procedure.","A materially equivalent statement of the Burden of Proof in Dismissal Cases is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Burden of Proof in Dismissal Cases.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Bare allegations do not shift the initial burden, and constructive dismissal requires proof that continued work became unreasonable, unlikely, or involved prohibited demotion or discrimination.

rows.subject: Labor Law and Social Legislation
rows.canonical_meaning: In assessing dismissal, an employer may consider a worker’s relevant prior infractions together with the current offense when they are sufficiently related and the total penalty remains proportionate.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Related past violations may matter, but they cannot be piled on arbitrarily to justify an excessive penalty.
rows.required_concepts: ["related prior violations may be considered","penalty must remain proportionate"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Related past violations may matter, but they cannot be piled on arbitrarily to justify an excessive penalty.","A materially equivalent statement of the Totality of Infractions Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Totality of Infractions Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: Remote, dissimilar, already condoned, or inadequately proved incidents cannot automatically convert a minor present offense into just cause.

rows.subject: Labor Law and Social Legislation
rows.canonical_meaning: Reinstatement may exceptionally yield to separation pay when genuine, serious hostility makes continued employment impracticable, but strained relations cannot be presumed from litigation or the employer’s refusal to reinstate.
rows.plain_language_meaning: Real, severe workplace hostility may justify separation pay instead of return to work, but filing a case alone is not enough.
rows.required_concepts: ["reinstatement is the ordinary remedy","genuine and serious strain may exceptionally justify separation pay"]
rows.accepted_paraphrases: ["Real, severe workplace hostility may justify separation pay instead of return to work, but filing a case alone is not enough.","A materially equivalent statement of the Strained Relations Doctrine is acceptable without the exact case name or section number."]
rows.material_contradictions: ["States the opposite of the Strained Relations Doctrine.","Treats a qualified rule as absolute or omits a condition that changes the legal result."]
rows.exceptions_or_limits: The doctrine is applied narrowly, especially to rank-and-file workers, lest an employer profit from its own illegal dismissal.
rows.primary_authority: BPI Employees Union-Davao City-FUBU v. Bank of the Philippine Islands

rows.subject: Labor Law and Social Legislation
rows.canonical_meaning: Employees who perform substantially equal work under similar conditions should receive equal pay unless a distinction rests on a substantial, job-related, and lawful basis rather than prohibited discrimination.
rows.plain_language_meaning: People doing substantially the same work should not be paid differently without a real lawful reason tied to the job.
rows.required_concepts: ["substantially equal work and conditions","pay distinction requires a substantial lawful basis"]
